facts.raw_span: A 64-year-old woman
20-year history of hypertension
dizziness and head discomfort of 3 days’ duration
blood pressure at presentation was 190/100 mmHg
no gastrointestinal symptoms
4.7 cm × 4.4 cm hypoechoic lesion with a clear, regular boundary
located between the upper pole of the spleen and the abdominal aorta
without detectable blood flow
5.5 cm × 4.3 cm smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass in the gastric wall
marked enhancement and surrounding lymph-node enlargement
smooth, hemispherical submucosal elevation on the gastric fundus
hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria

concepts.why: The presence of a hypoechoic lesion with a clear boundary and a smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass in the gastric wall suggests GIST.

concepts.why: The marked enhancement and surrounding lymph-node enlargement could suggest gastric lymphoma.

support_spans: 5.5 cm × 4.3 cm smoothly marginated soft-tissue mass in the gastric wall
hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria
concepts.why: The presence of spindle cells with areas of calcification on EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration suggests a spindle cell tumor.
The location of the lesion between the upper pole of the spleen and the abdominal aorta is consistent with a gastric paraganglioma.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a hypoechoic, heterogeneous mass arising from the muscularis propria with marked enhancement and surrounding lymph-node enlargement, as well as the EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration findings, decided it.
